standard_prerequisites.name: Admissible short exact sequence of dg modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: A short exact sequence of dg modules splitting as graded modules, with the associated maps between the outer and middle terms.
standard_prerequisites.use: The three sequences provide the maps whose images and kernels are compared (source lines 843-844, 873-874).

standard_prerequisites.name: Commuting up to homotopy and strict commutation
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two squares of dg module maps commute up to homotopy; a map homotopic to a strictly commuting one can be substituted.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis says the two squares commute up to homotopy and the proof replaces the maps by homotopic ones making the relevant squares commute strictly (source lines 845-865, 870-872).

standard_prerequisites.name: Replacement lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a square commutes up to homotopy and one of its horizontal maps is an admissible monomorphism, then the vertical map can be replaced by a homotopic one making the square commute (the author's lemma lemma-make-commute-map, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked to obtain the strict squares, first for b and then for b' (source line 870).

core_obligations: Replace the maps by homotopic ones: apply the retained lemma lemma-make-commute-map to the left diagram for b and to the right diagram for b', so that the relevant squares commute strictly (source lines 870-872).

Read off the two containments: translate the strict commutation into the statement that the image of b is contained in the image of K_2 in L_2 and the kernel of b' contains that image (source lines 872-874).
Conclude: deduce that the composite b' b is the zero map of modules, hence homotopic to zero (source lines 874-875).

proof_roadmap.step: Replace b and b' by homotopic maps making the relevant squares commute strictly.
Translate strict commutation into the image and kernel containments.
Conclude b' b = 0, hence homotopic to zero.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-nilpotent at source lines 840-867: for a dg algebra A, three admissible short exact sequences 0 -> K_i -> L_i -> M_i -> 0 indexed by i = 1,2,3, and maps b : L_1 -> L_2 and b' : L_2 -> L_3 whose two squares commute up to homotopy, the composite b' b is homotopic to zero. The proof at source lines 869-876 is short but it is the step that makes the maps of triangles rigid: it invokes the author's lemma on homotopy commutative squares twice, once for each square cum triangle, to replace b and b' by homotopic maps for which the relevant squares commute strictly, and then translates the strict commutativity into the two containments of images and kernels that force b' b to be the zero map of modules. The substance is the reduction from commuting up to homotopy to commuting on the nose, and the observation that the two containments make the composite vanish; the statement mentions neither. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
